subject: Private control plane: operator access model & IdP/SCIM constraints
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Okta IdP Team <okta-infra@acme-corp.com>, security-eng@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private control plane: operator access model & IdP/SCIM constraints

Hi --

Following our onboarding questionnaire, a few constraints on Acme's side will affect how we integrate IdP and provisioning for the Private Control Plane deployment in their VPC:

- Control plane endpoints are reachable only from within the Acme VPC (no public inbound).
- IdP (Okta) sits in Acme's corporate network and cannot directly reach our control plane.
- Acme prefers SCIM pushes for provisioning but will only allow SCIM traffic over an internal proxy or from a vetted partner IP range.
- Auditing team requires operator role assignments to be traceable to short-lived assertions (no long-lived shared keys).

We propose a small design review to align on one of two options:

A) IdP Assertion Proxy (recommended)
  - Deploy a lightweight assertion-proxy inside Acme VPC (customer-managed) that terminates SAML and forwards signed assertions to the private control plane.
  - Proxy rotates a client cert to the control plane; Redwood validates assertions and exchanges them for short-lived operator tokens.

B) Gateway + Scheduled SCIM Bridge
  - A scheduled, outbound-only SCIM bridge (from a VM in Acme) that pushes user/group state to Redwood over a TLS tunnel.
  - Operator role mapping via SCIM group attributes; requires periodic reconciliation.

Attachment: privcp_operator_access_matrix.xlsx (matrix of proposed roles, SCIM attributes and minimum required claims)

Can Okta/integration folks confirm whether option A is feasible given your network posture? If not, we can detail option B and call out the trade-offs for auditability and time-to-provision.

Scheduling: I'm available Wed/Thu next week for a 45 min tech sync.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private control plane: operator access model & IdP/SCIM constraints

Camila,

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from Acme IdP side:

- We can host an assertion-proxy inside the VPC (we've done this for several partners) but it needs to be lightweight and run in a private subnet w/ NAT egress only.
- Outbound-only connectivity means the proxy can reach Redwood's control plane endpoints but only over TLS to a whitelisted endpoint.
- For SCIM we can do push provisioning, but security requires mTLS from our bridge VM to your SCIM endpoint — we will not allow bearer tokens without mutual TLS.
- For operator role assignment, we prefer SCIM group -> role mapping for consistent audit trails; however, JIT via SAML assertion is acceptable if assertions include the role/grant claim and a unique assertion id for trace correlation.

Open questions:
1) Can Redwood accept assertions proxied from a customer-managed VM and validate via your public cert exchange process?
2) What is your recommended TTL for the short-lived operator tokens? Our security team prefers <= 1 hour.

We can join a design call Wed 2027-11-03 10:00 PT — propose to invite our network engineer and security compliance lead.

--
Acme Okta Team

All — quick tech notes ahead of the sync:

1) Assertion proxy flow (our recommended path):
   - Acme runs an assertion-proxy (docker) in the private subnet. Proxy terminates SAML with Okta and signs a forwarding JWT using a customer-managed key.
   - Proxy makes an HTTPS call to https://privcp.redwood-inference.com/assert with the signed JWT. Our control plane validates signature against cert(s) exchanged during onboarding, maps incoming claims to operator roles and issues a short-lived operator token (STS style) back to the proxy.
   - Operator sessions created using that token are logged in the control plane audit log with assertion_id and the originating proxy IP.

2) SCIM considerations (fallback):
   - For pilot we can accept a scoped SCIM service account with bearer token, but it must be rotated immediately after pilot and replaced by mTLS-configured bridge for production.
   - Attribute mapping: scim.attribute:groups -> role.name; scim.attribute:employeeNumber -> operator.external_id. See scim_attribute_mapping.yml (attached).

3) IAM role TTL: We recommend 15m-60m depending on operation sensitivity; default 1 hour if Acme security is okay with it.

Attachment: scim_attribute_mapping.yml

I'll bring a sequence diagram to the call and a minimal onboarding checklist (cert exchange steps, cert formats, sample assertion).

Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Camila / Ben —

Thanks for the options. A few ask items from Acme Security before we finalize the architecture:

- Provide a network flow diagram showing connector/proxy placement, which subnets need outbound access, and what ports are required. We need to run this through our firewall policy review.
- Provide proof that control plane will not accept assertion replay — we need nonce/assertion_id replay protection and clear logging for correlation to our SIEM.
- Can Redwood commit to token TTL <= 1 hour for operator tokens for the pilot?
- Legal: can Redwood sign the standard Partner Addendum (we'll send the doc) — they prefer a data processing addendum (DPA) plus SOC2.

We will also include Rackspace ops (ops@rackspace.com) in the call; they will help if a partner-managed bridging instance is required for VPC network peering.

Regards,

All —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear asks. Summary and agreed next-steps: 

Decisions:
- Pilot path: Option A (Assertion Proxy) + scoped SCIM fallback for day-0 provisioning.
- Token TTL: 1 hour for all operator tokens during pilot (Agreed).
- Replay protection: Redwood will require assertion_id + timestamp in inbound JWT and will persist assertion_id to prevent replay; we will include nonce verification in the onboarding checklist.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Ben: sequence diagram + minimal cert exchange checklist (uploaded to Drive) — ETA: 2027-11-10 EOD.
- Okta/Acme IdP: confirm whether their proxy will present mTLS client certs to privcp endpoint or whether the proxy will only sign forwarding JWTs — please confirm by 2027-11-12.
- Camila: draft PS estimate for partner-managed proxy deployment + day-0 support (will share before EOD 11/10).
- Laura: capture commercial fallback for a scoped SCIM service account for the pilot.
- Acme Security: share Partner Addendum (DPA) and list of firewall rules they will need to approve — ETA: 2027-11-12.

I'll schedule the 45 min tech sync for 2027-11-10 10:00 PT and share the calendar invite (link in related_links). Please add any missing items.

Best,
